html:
The Indian farmers' protest was a year long movement against three farm laws passed in September 2020. Tens of thousands of farmers, most from Punjab and Haryana, camped on the highways at the edges of Delhi from November 2020 until December 2021.

The laws let private traders buy crops outside the regulated government markets and allowed contract farming. The government of Narendra Modi said they would free farmers. Farmers feared they would end the state markets and the minimum support price at which the government buys wheat and rice, a system set up during the Green Revolution that Punjab's farms depend on.

Through a cold winter and the Covid wave, the farmers kept up their sit ins with community kitchens and tractors, and hundreds of protesters died during the year. Unions joined under the Samyukt Kisan Morcha. In January 2021 the Supreme Court suspended the laws. On 19 November 2021 Modi announced their repeal, a rare retreat, and the camps broke up in December.
